record.paper_title: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
record.original_question: For the stochastic M/G/k queue with arrivals over time, outside the heavy-traffic regime typical optimality results do not apply. Under what conditions is SRPT-k actually optimal for minimizing mean response time?

evidence.quote: Outside of heavy traffic, understanding when SRPT-k is optimal and analyzing its performance are both big open problems.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an M/G/k queueing system: jobs arrive according to a Poisson process of rate λ and have i.i.d. service requirements drawn from a general distribution G, served by k identical parallel servers (each of unit speed). Job sizes are known to the scheduler upon arrival, and the scheduler may preempt jobs at any time without cost. The SRPT-k policy assigns the k servers, at every instant, to the (at most) k jobs in the system with the smallest remaining processing requirements.

Let ρ = λ E[G]/k denote the system load, and let E[T] denote the steady-state mean response time (time from arrival to completion).

Determine necessary and/or sufficient conditions on the service-time distribution G, the number of servers k, and the load ρ — outside the heavy-traffic limit ρ → 1 — under which the SRPT-k policy minimizes the steady-state mean response time E[T] over all (possibly preemptive, size-aware) scheduling policies. In particular, decide whether SRPT-k is optimal for minimizing mean response time in the M/G/k queue at low or moderate load, and if not, characterize the gap to optimality.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to be open. Stochastic bounds and asymptotic optimality of SRPT-k in the heavy-traffic limit (ρ → 1) have been established (Grosof, Scully, Harchol-Balter), and an explicit open problem on M/G/k/SRPT under medium load was posed in Stochastic Systems (2020). Subsequent work (e.g., SIGMETRICS 2024) provides improved bounds and shows that SRPT-k can be strictly improved upon under moderate load, but the question of when SRPT-k is exactly optimal for minimizing mean response time outside heavy traffic remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Open Problem—M/G/k/SRPT Under Medium Load
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds on mean response time of M/G/k/SRPT in heavy traffic have been proven, leaving open the question of mean response time under medium load.
status_evidence.claim: Optimality/analysis of SRPT-k outside heavy traffic is explicitly stated as open.

status_evidence.title: Bounds on M/G/k Scheduling Under Moderate Load Improving on SRPT-k
status_evidence.snippet: Improving on SRPT-k and tightening lower bounds under moderate load.
status_evidence.claim: SRPT-k is not optimal under moderate load; improvements have been demonstrated.

status_evidence.title: SRPT for multiserver systems
status_evidence.snippet: First stochastic bound on response time of SRPT-k and asymptotic optimality in the heavy-traffic limit.
status_evidence.claim: Only the heavy-traffic asymptotic optimality of SRPT-k is established.
